key_insight: Tuning the shared tether between two square resonators controls frequency splitting and can enhance symmetric-mode dissipation dilution beyond that of an isolated polygon.
engineering_relevance: Coupler geometry offers a design lever for coupled mechanical resonators with tunable mode separation and reduced dissipation.
method: Develop a continuum model linking coupler length and width to mode splitting and dissipation dilution.
Compare analytical predictions with finite element simulations.
Derive short-coupler mode behavior and a short-coupler, short-tether expression for Q·f.
evidence_signal: For a 100 μm-long, 2 μm-wide coupler, finite element calculations yield 17.7 Hz frequency splitting and symmetric-mode dilution approximately 13% above the analytical isolated-polygon value.
watch_item: The simplified loss and Q·f expressions rely on short-coupler or short-tether limits, and the abstract reports simulation comparisons rather than experimental validation.
paper_title: Coupled Soft-Clamped Polygon Resonators with Tunable Mechanical Coupling
